description: A freelance designer must decide whether to accept a photographer's offer to trade a promotional poster for a family photo session, while an event organizer and a former client help settle the exact deliverables and rights for the swap.

shared_context.S1: Cal has offered Rina a family photo session in exchange for a promotional poster for his weekend pop-up photo booth.
shared_context.S2: Rina decides whether to proceed and sets the final terms of the service swap.
shared_context.S3: The poster will promote Cal's photo booth at an upcoming neighborhood event and may incorporate selected photos from Rina's session.
shared_context.S4: This gathering is the final review of the swap: each participant gives one concise report on the details they know when their turn comes, and Rina settles the complete terms before the conversation ends; no later meeting is planned.
shared_context.S5: The final terms must state separately that Cal grants Rina rights to use the session photos, and that Rina provides Cal the poster for his event promotion.

PF1.text: Cal is available to conduct the family photo session only on Saturday, June 15, and he can deliver exactly 40 edited digital photos by June 20. When reporting his session details during this final review, Cal should use a formal reveal of PF1.

PF2.text: Mei confirmed with the event printer that the poster must be an 18-by-24-inch PDF at 300 dpi, and the printer needs 100 copies.

PF3.text: Jonah previously hired Cal and learned that Cal's usual package grants only personal-use rights for the photos; promotional use of those photos requires an explicit perpetual license, which Jonah did not receive on his own booking.

acceptance_conditions: The swap must proceed as a poster-design-for-family-photo-session exchange.
The photo session must be scheduled for Saturday, June 15.
The settlement must provide exactly 40 edited digital photos by June 20.
The poster must be specified as 18 inches by 24 inches in PDF format at 300 dpi.
The settlement must include exactly 100 printed copies of the poster.
The promotional license field must explicitly record that Cal grants Rina a perpetual promotional license for photos from the session.
A commitment must record Cal granting Rina that perpetual promotional license for the session photos.
The license requirement must cite PF3 as justification.

content_checks.C4: decisions['poster_width_inches'] == 18 and decisions['poster_height_inches'] == 24 and decisions['poster_file_type'] == 'PDF' and decisions['poster_resolution_dpi'] == 300
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'photo_license_grant' and c['target'] == 'Rina' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF3' in revealed and any(c['type'] == 'photo_license_grant' and c['target'] == 'Rina' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Cal's private availability changes the session date to exactly Saturday, June 15 and changes the deliverable to exactly 40 edited photos delivered by June 20.
The printer's requirements change the poster specification to exactly 18 by 24 inches, PDF, 300 dpi, and exactly 100 printed copies.

Jonah's prior booking changes the license from ordinary personal use to an explicit perpetual promotional license granted by Cal to Rina for the session photos, requiring a matching commitment and citation.
